key_insight: This paper shows that a chiral 2D halide perovskite can detect telecom-band circularly polarized light through third-harmonic-generation circular dichroism, revealing hidden giant chiral anisotropy that is only visible with polarization-resolved measurements.
engineering_relevance: The work points to perovskite-based chiral photonic devices for telecom-wavelength sensing, optical information processing, encryption, and anti-counterfeiting.
method: Studied (R/S-MBACl)2PbI4, a chiral two-dimensional halide perovskite.
Performed polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation measurements to separate orthogonal THG channels.
Compared total-THG detection with channel-resolved analysis to expose hidden circular dichroism.
evidence_signal: Polarization-resolved data revealed opposite-handed chiral NLO responses in orthogonal channels, and the separated dissymmetry factors exceeded 1.9, much larger than conventional total-THG evaluation.
watch_item: The giant THG-CD is underestimated if only total THG intensity is measured, so device characterization must include polarization-resolved detection to avoid misleading conclusions.
paper_title: Telecom-band Chiral Light Detection through Hidden Giant Third-Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Two-dimensional Halide Perovskite
